label: original-phase input of b, z, or h
explanation: Token detector for the letters b, z and h when they are input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It never fires on any other token, the delimiter, or copy-phase steps, with one exception: weak activations (about 0.2 of max) when b/z/h is fed back as the first copied token (t = L+1), which make up about 1.4% of mass. Magnitude depends on the token, b > z > h (b gives about 49% of mass, h about 18%, at similar counts), and is highest at t=0: b at t=0 hits the maximum. Repeat occurrences in the same sequence fire more weakly. Activation does not depend on L or on which tokens come before.

issues: The claim that repeat occurrences fire at 'a much lower rate (in_first=0)' is misleading. The low in_first=0 rate in the profile (0.014) comes from copy-phase steps, where most inputs are repeats. Inside the original phase, repeat b/z/h fire just as reliably as first occurrences: the predicate isin(b,z,h) & phase==0 & in_first==0 has test precision 0.9935, against 0.9933 for in_first==1. Repeat b alone has precision 1.0 over 9790 steps. Repeats may fire with smaller magnitude (the examples show 0.58-0.94 against 1.00 at t=0), but that is mixed up with position t, and the rate claim is wrong.

There is a small, mildly systematic set of false positives: h in the original phase is sometimes inactive, especially right after c ('c h'), where precision is 0.874 over 2982 steps. Precision for h overall in the original phase is 0.980, against 1.0 for b. This is about 0.7% of predicted steps, so it does not hurt the label.

Missed activations are copy-phase only and weak (about 0.2 of max), 1.4% of activation mass. Most are b/z/h fed back at recall_idx==1 (10785 of 13385 copy-phase activations on dev), which matches the explanation. In the copy phase the feature never fires on tokens other than b/z/h (precision 0.0 for phase==2 & not b/z/h).

Other claims check out on test: precision 0.993, recall 0.960, F1 0.976, mass recall 0.986. It never fires on the delimiter or on other tokens. Mass split is b 0.49, z 0.33, h 0.18. The t=0 mass share (0.206) is the highest, with the top examples all b at t=0. Firing rate is flat across L (lift 1.0x everywhere) and shows no lift from prev_tok or prev2_tok. Adding the recall_idx==1 steps gives precision 0.889, recall 0.992, F1 0.938, as reported.
